entry.title: Titans vs. Colts odds: Opening lines for Week 6 matchup
entry.summary: Posts like this are getting tougher and tougher to write. The Tennessee Titans opened as a 6.5-point underdog on the road against the Indianapolis Colts at FanDuel Sportsbook. Even though the Colts have two wins, they aren’t as good as the Houston Texans. Does that mean the Titans have a chance to win this game? […]
entry.content:
Posts like this are getting tougher and tougher to write. The Tennessee Titans opened as a 6.5-point underdog on the road against the Indianapolis Colts at FanDuel Sportsbook. Even though the Colts have two wins, they aren’t as good as the Houston Texans. Does that mean the Titans have a chance to win this game? Not based on anything we have seen so far this season.

The Colts defense hasn’t been very good. They are in the bottom third of the league against both the pass and the run. Is this a get right spot for Cam Ward and the offense? Let’s not get crazy here. We have seen very little so far to give us any indication that such a spot exists.

The day after the Titans get embarrassed by the Texans someone usually gets fired. The problem this year is that everyone is so new, there is no obvious person to take the fall, but hey, surely Amy Adams Strunk can find someone.

entry.title: Titans get embarrassed 26-3 by Texans: Quick recap
entry.summary: Being a fan of the Tennessee Titans is not for the faint of heart. The NFL is set up for teams to turn around very quickly. The Titans have not been able to do that. On Thursday, November 17th, the Titans beat the Green Bay Packers on the road. They had also won the previous […]
entry.content:
Being a fan of the Tennessee Titans is not for the faint of heart. The NFL is set up for teams to turn around very quickly. The Titans have not been able to do that. On Thursday, November 17th, the Titans beat the Green Bay Packers on the road. They had also won the previous week against the Denver Broncos. That is the last time they won back-to-back games. Since then, the Titans are 12-51.

The most disheartening thing is that there is no sign of things getting any better. What is there to say about the game today? The offense is just terrible. Last week, we saw a huge game from Carnell Tate. This week, he had just one catch for six yards on five targets. The Texans were able to completely erase him from the game. Whose fault is that? Tate’s? Cam Ward’s? Brian Daboll’s? The answer is probably yes.

This game didn’t surprise me. There were a lot of people who thought the Titans had a chance to win. I was not one of those people. I’ll be surprised at this point if they don’t go 0-17.

There are people that are already cheering for a draft pick. I am not one of those people. This is an important game for Robert Saleh’s Tennessee Titans. He is trying to build a winning culture. You cannot do that if you never win.

The Titans can pretty much end the Texans’ season if they beat them today. That’s something this team can build on for the rest of the season. Plus, it is always fun to beat the Temu Titans.

entry.title: NFL predictions: Who gets their first win in the Titans-Texans matchup?
entry.summary: The 0-4 Houston Texans travel to Nashville to take on the 0-4 Tennessee Titans on Sunday. It’s not a huge surprise that the Titans are 0-4, but a lot of people thought the Texans were going to be Super Bowl contenders this season. That feels like a long shot at 0-4. It would be virtually […]
entry.content:
The 0-4 Houston Texans travel to Nashville to take on the 0-4 Tennessee Titans on Sunday. It’s not a huge surprise that the Titans are 0-4, but a lot of people thought the Texans were going to be Super Bowl contenders this season. That feels like a long shot at 0-4. It would be virtually impossible at 0-5.

On paper, the Texans are a much better team. Their defensive front is one of the best in the league. The Titans offensive line has played much better this year, but they have not faced a front like this to this point. This will be a really good test for that unit.

I’d love to call an upset here, but I just don’t see it. The Titans are going to get the Texans’ best shot with their season on the line. Cam Ward played better last week than the week before, but he is going to be under more pressure this week. We have seen that when he feels pressure, he has the tendency to revert to some bad habits that create inconsistent play. Look for the Texans to get at least 4 sacks of Ward in this one.

On defense, the key to stopping the Texans is stopping Nico Collins. The Texans average over 30 points per game when Collins plays and under 12 points per game when he doesn’t. Obviously, it isn’t exactly that simple, but those are the facts. The Titans will be without starting safety Amani Hooker. While Hooker hasn’t exactly been lights out this season, the secondary is better with him on the field.

Collins is +144 to get 90 yards receiving in this game over at FanDuel Sportsbook. That feels like free money to me.

Score prediction: Texans 27 Titans 13

entry.title: 3 Titans who will be tested vs. Texans in Week 5
entry.summary: The winless Tennessee Titans (0-4) are playing versus the winless Houston Texans (0-4) in Week 5. Many expected the Titans to struggle. The Texans’ are however shockingly bad (and bringing Tennessee fans some joy). Nonetheless, everyone expects the Texans to dominate this game. The Titans will need big-time performances from certain players to execute the […]
entry.content:
The winless Tennessee Titans (0-4) are playing versus the winless Houston Texans (0-4) in Week 5. Many expected the Titans to struggle. The Texans’ are however shockingly bad (and bringing Tennessee fans some joy).

Nonetheless, everyone expects the Texans to dominate this game. The Titans will need big-time performances from certain players to execute the upset. We’ve identified three Titans players who particularly need strong showings.

WR Carnell Tate

Titans rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate enjoyed a breakout performance in Week 4, registering nine receptions for 145 yards. Can the fourth overall pick keep momentum going? Tate will be up against a good Texans secondary that is currently underperforming. No. 1 Texans cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. is among the premier coverage defenders in the NFL. The Titans’ passing game will definitely be under pressure.

LT Dan Moore Jr.

The Titans’ offensive line has shockingly exceeded expectations. Position coach Carmen Bricillo has done an outstanding job with this unit. The latest composite rankings has the Titans’ protection ranking fifth-best in the league. Quarterback Cam Ward has only been sacked six times in four games. Left tackle Dan Moore Jr. has been pretty good. He (and his teammates) will be tested by Danielle Hunter, Jadeveon Clowney, and Will Anderson Jr.

CB Alontae Taylor

Texans No. 1 receiver Nico Collins returned from injury in Week 4 and put forth a dominant performance. He recorded seven receptions on eight targets for 118 yards and two touchdowns in a hard-fought loss to the Dallas Cowboys. C.J. Stroud looked Collins’ way every time Nick Caley’s offense needed a big play. The Titans’ secondary has been nowhere near good enough in coverage this season. Robert Saleh’s No. 1 cornerback is Alontae Taylor. The Titans don’t follow WRs, but it’ll likely be Taylor who often draws the Collins assignment.

entry.title: Titans-Texans: Not all 0-4 teams are created equal
entry.summary: On paper, it appears the Tennessee Titans have a winnable game versus the Houston Texans in Week 5. Both AFC South teams are 0-4. Despite that, the Texans are considered heavy favorites despite the showdown being contested at Nissan Stadium. Both organizations found themselves in familiar territory last season. They entered their first matchup (Week […]
entry.content:
On paper, it appears the Tennessee Titans have a winnable game versus the Houston Texans in Week 5. Both AFC South teams are 0-4. Despite that, the Texans are considered heavy favorites despite the showdown being contested at Nissan Stadium.

Both organizations found themselves in familiar territory last season. They entered their first matchup (Week 4) sharing 0-3 records. This was the first game then-Titans HC Brian Callahan lost play-calling duties. The Texans enjoyed a dominant 26-0 win. Hopefully Sunday doesn’t repeat that result.

That victory jumpstarted a Texans turnaround. They finished 12-5 and qualified for the playoffs. The Texans hope this is another get-right game versus the Titans.

The Texans lost two high-scoring affairs with the Buffalo Bills and Dallas Cowboys. They were disappointing in losses to the Cincinnati Bengals and Indianapolis Colts. It’s worth noting star receiver Nico Collins missed the Bengals and Colts games. They are averaging 30 PPG with Collins in the lineup.

The Texans lost two shootouts with the high-octane Bills and Cowboys. The Bengals are another postseason contender. They’ve faced a pretty tough schedule so far. The Titans are unfortunately nowhere near as difficult of a matchup on paper.

The Texans have had a surprising amount of issues on defense. Head coach DeMeco Ryans recently announced he’s taking defensive play-calling duties back from coordinator Matt Burke. That’s probably bad news for this Titans offense. Nobody knows the Texans defense better than Coach Ryans does.

Brian Daboll’s offense found something between Cam Ward and Carnell Tate in Week 4. CeeDee Lamb torched this Texans secondary on that same afternoon. The Titans need to move Tate around the formation, and target him 10+ times on Sunday.

The Titans-Texans rivalry lives on, especially after the rebranding followed Oilers themes. Owner Amy Adams Strunk will be paying close attention to Sunday’s result. Hopefully the Titans make it a competitive game.
